findings: Chapter 3 exercise (PDF 71-74, printed 68-71) solved 2026-10-29 on the owner's request (Practice, English and Roman Urdu): 10 MCQs (keyed checkpoints), 9 short answers, 10 constructed response questions, 7 comprehensive questions and 10 numerical problems, all as printed and in the book's order. Drafts for the academic review.
The book prints no MCQ key; the keys were worked out from the chapter: 3.1 d, 3.2 b, 3.3 a, 3.4 a, 3.5 b, 3.6 d, 3.7 c, 3.8 c, 3.9 d, 3.10 a.

Book corrections: Comprehensive 3.3 asks to prove torque = I x angular momentum; it should be angular acceleration (tau = I alpha). Numerical 3.6 prints 28.8 kg m^2 (diameter used as radius); with r = 0.30 m, I = (2/5)Mr^2 = 7.2 kg m^2. Numerical 3.7 prints 7.78 km h^-1; the unit should be km s^-1 (v = 7.79 km s^-1 with G = 6.67e-11, M = 6.0e24 kg).

Unreadable: the power of ten in the printed answer of Numerical 3.1 is not legible; the computed answer is 6.6 x 10^-11 rad (the prompt says the exponent is not legible). The Earth-moon distance is read as 3.8 x 10^8 m.

Answers beyond the chapter: CRQ 3.4 uses the simple pendulum formula T = 2 pi sqrt(l/g) (earlier class); CRQ 3.8 uses the resultant (relative) velocity of rain and wind; Short 3.6 (double rear tyres: load sharing, grip, safety) is general knowledge. Comprehensive 3.4 gives T = 2 pi sqrt(R/g) = 5.08 x 10^3 s (about 85 min), where the chapter's worked value is 5060 s (about 84 min).
Short 3.6 prints 'rare wheels' for 'rear wheels'; explained in a Roman Urdu Wazahat box. No figures are needed; nothing is copied from the book beyond the printed questions.
